comments.body:
## Root cause confirmed: blue-green autodeploy omits the gate-scratch configuration that compose sets

Read-only investigation complete. The growth is **accumulated gate snapshot data landing on a container writable layer instead of the dedicated scratch volume**, caused by a config-parity gap between the compose definition and the blue-green `docker run` path.

### Attribution

`docker inspect --size` at 18:36 PDT, summing to the CloudWatch numerator of 1,939,074,618 B:

| Container | State | `SizeRw` |
|---|---|---:|
| `rebar-mcp-4f12815e9a0b-8092` | running | 1,341,684,890 B |
| `compose-gerrit-1` | running | 597,357,970 B |
| `compose-review-bot-1` | running | 31,326 B |
| `compose-opcert-1` | running | 432 B |

`container_exited_bytes = 0` is consistent — all 4 containers are running, so the reaper genuinely has nothing to reclaim.

### What the bytes are

Inside `rebar-mcp-4f12815e9a0b-8092`, the upperdir is dominated by `/tmp/rebar-gate-snapshots`, measuring 3,465,011,200 B by `du`. The largest contributors are ticket-store snapshots:

- `tickets-04420b1c70e47066cea90eb0365ba43fe4d56108` — 1,595,334,656 B
- 9 further `tickets-*` directories at roughly 189–212 MB each
- code snapshots: `4f12815…` at 64 MB, plus smaller `71a719…` and `cab36…`

The largest repeated files are `.tickets-tracker.index` (~33.8 MB each), `.bridge_state/bindings.json` (~22.2 MB each), and copied repo artifacts.

This is snapshot artifact data. Not logs, not Docker build cache.

### The defect

`/opt/rebar/infra/compose/docker-compose.yml` sets `REBAR_GATE_TMPDIR=/var/lib/rebar/gate-scratch` and `TMPDIR=/var/lib/rebar/gate-scratch`. The live MCP container has **neither**.

`infra/scripts/autodeploy.sh:mcp_run_new` builds blue-green MCP containers with `docker run` and mirrors many compose environment variables — but not `REBAR_GATE_TMPDIR`, not `TMPDIR`, and not the gate-scratch bind. So every gate snapshot writes to the container's own writable layer.

The scratch volume itself is present and healthy: `/var/lib/rebar/gate-scratch` on `/dev/nvme2n1`, 5% used. It is simply not being used by this container.

### Correcting the urgency stated when this was filed

The filing claimed roughly 2 hours of headroom by analogy to bug `3276`. That was wrong, and the metric detail is why.

`container_writable_used_percent` is measured against `DOCKER_CONTAINER_WRITABLE_BYTES = 2,147,483,648` — a **configured share ceiling**, not free disk. With `container_quota_enforceable = 0` the host cannot enforce that ceiling, so crossing 100% produces an alarm and nothing else. Root still has roughly 40 GB free, so at the observed rate actual exhaustion is on the order of weeks, not hours.

That makes this materially different from `3276`, which was real root-volume exhaustion. Severity should be reconsidered against that; the defect is real and the fix is small, but it is not an imminent outage.

### Restart behaviour and bounds

A `docker restart` would **not** reset the growth — the same writable layer persists. Recreating the container would discard the snapshots, since they are not in a volume or bind mount, but accumulation restarts immediately unless the run-path gap is closed.

Nothing currently bounds the growth. The exited-container reaper cannot reach a running container. Overlay2 quota is unavailable (`CAP_CHECK_QUOTA=0`). The snapshot janitor is running — it touches `/tmp/rebar-gate-snapshots/gc/last-pass.stamp` — but without the scratch-volume and watermark settings in the live environment it is not enforcing a writable-share ceiling.

### Inflection

The 16:00 local trigger is **not determinable** from retained evidence. Verified: the container started 10:08 PDT with early snapshots at 10:10–11:18, then added ticket snapshots during active gate use at 17:23, 18:01, 18:14, and 18:37 PDT. That is consistent with resumed gate workload after 17:00, but which session initiated each gate was not established, and at least two authorized sessions are active.

### Remedy direction

Close the parity gap in `mcp_run_new` so it carries `REBAR_GATE_TMPDIR`, `TMPDIR`, and the gate-scratch bind exactly as compose does, then roll the MCP backend so future snapshots land on the dedicated volume.

Recreating the container now would drop the accumulated layer, but that is temporary and not a fix. Enabling overlay2 quotas would give a hard per-container ceiling, but needs host filesystem support and a reboot, and would not correct the wrong scratch target.

### Amplifier worth noting

A single tickets snapshot is 1.6 GB, and the `.tickets-tracker.index` copies are ~33.8 MB each. Snapshot cost scales directly with tickets-store size, which bug `3394` tracks as growing. Reducing store size shrinks every future snapshot.

Nothing was reaped, pruned, restarted, deleted, or reconfigured. No repository changes.

compiled_state.description:
## Problem

Gate snapshots written by the on-box MCP container land on the container's own writable layer at `/tmp/rebar-gate-snapshots` instead of the dedicated gate-scratch EBS volume. `rebar-mcp-4f12815e9a0b-8092` holds 1,341,684,890 B of writable layer, dominated by that directory (3,465,011,200 B by `du`, largest single entry a 1,595,334,656 B tickets-store snapshot). This drove `rebar-container-writable-usage-high` to ALARM at 90.3% of the configured 2 GiB share ceiling.

Root-cause evidence is in the investigation comment on this ticket.

## Cause

The MCP service is **not configured for gate scratch in either deployment path**.

Four settings govern where gate snapshots land:

- `REBAR_GATE_TMPDIR` — the content-addressed snapshot store's base directory, read by `rebar._snapshot.repo_snapshot.peek_store_root`.
- `TMPDIR` — the system temp dir, followed by `tempfile.TemporaryDirectory`. Compose documents these as two distinct consumers and warns that setting only one "leaves half the bytes on root".
- `REBAR_GATE_FREE_WATERMARK_PCT` — the snapshot janitor's volume-relative reclaim trigger. Without it the janitor falls back to a disk-size-blind absolute threshold, which is why the janitor is running yet bounding nothing.
- A bind of `/var/lib/rebar` making the scratch volume reachable.

In `infra/compose/docker-compose.yml` all four appear **only** under `services.review-bot` (lines 257, 276, 277, 313). The `mcp` service block sets none of them. `infra/scripts/autodeploy.sh:mcp_run_new`, which creates the live blue-green MCP containers with `docker run`, also sets none of them.

So the ADR 0112 decision 3 / story `aa40-cbda-ee38-481c` gate-scratch fix was applied to the review-bot service alone. The MCP service also runs gates and produces snapshots — it is the container holding the 1.3 GB — and was never brought onto the scratch volume.

The scratch volume itself is healthy and 5% used at `/var/lib/rebar/gate-scratch` on `/dev/nvme2n1`. It is simply not mounted into this container.

### Correction to this plan's earlier framing

An earlier revision of this plan described the defect as `mcp_run_new` drifting from settings compose already had for the MCP service. That was wrong: the quoted compose block is the **review-bot** service. Plan review caught it. The corrected scope below fixes both paths rather than aligning one to a source that does not exist.

## Why the ADR 0112 guard did not catch it

ADR 0112 forbids silent fallback to root, and gate admission decides whether the volume is mounted from a declaration marker on the root filesystem beside the mount point plus a proof marker inside it. Compose binds the **parent** `/var/lib/rebar` rather than the mount point so both markers are visible.

With no bind at all, the container sees neither marker, so the guard cannot distinguish "unmounted" from "not configured" and never fires. The guard is structurally blind to this case, so the fix is configuration plus a parity test, not a new guard.

## Approach

1. Add the four settings to the `mcp` service in `docker-compose.yml`, mirroring the review-bot values, as the single source of truth.
2. Mirror them in `mcp_run_new` so blue-green containers match.
3. Extend `tests/unit/test_gate_scratch_volume_aa40.py` to pin agreement between compose's **mcp** service, `autodeploy.sh`'s MCP run path, and the mount value the test already pins across terraform and `observability.sh`.

That test currently pins agreement only for the service that had the settings, which is why a service lacking them entirely raised nothing. Extending it is the fix for the class; the configuration alone fixes only the instance.

Test first: the added assertions must fail against the unmodified `docker-compose.yml` and `autodeploy.sh`, demonstrating they detect the real defect rather than passing vacuously.

Rolling the MCP backend to pick up the corrected run path is an operational follow-on performed after this lands, not part of this change.

## Severity note

This is **not** an imminent outage, contrary to the original filing, which compared it to bug `3276`. The percentage is measured against a configured share ceiling that `container_quota_enforceable = 0` means the host cannot enforce, so crossing 100% alarms and nothing more. Root has roughly 40 GB free. The defect is real and the fix is small, but the deadline is not hours.

## Out of scope

- Enabling overlay2 quota enforcement. It needs host filesystem support and a reboot, and would not correct the wrong scratch target.
- Recreating or restarting the running container. A restart does not reclaim the layer, and recreation without this fix merely restarts accumulation.
- Reducing tickets-store size, which scales every snapshot. Tracked by `3394`.
- The exited-container reaper, which works correctly and has nothing to reclaim.
- The review-bot service, which is already configured correctly.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] The `mcp` service in `infra/compose/docker-compose.yml` sets `REBAR_GATE_TMPDIR` to the same mount path the review-bot service uses. Verified by reading the mcp service block and comparing the value to line 276.
- [ ] The `mcp` service sets `TMPDIR` to that same mount path. Verified by reading the mcp service block and comparing the value to line 277.
- [ ] The `mcp` service sets `REBAR_GATE_FREE_WATERMARK_PCT` to the same value the review-bot service uses. Verified by comparing against line 257.
- [ ] The `mcp` service binds `/var/lib/rebar` at the parent path rather than at the mount point, so both ADR 0112 markers are visible. Verified by reading the mcp service volumes list.
- [ ] `infra/scripts/autodeploy.sh:mcp_run_new` passes all three environment variables with values matching the compose mcp service. Verified by `grep -c 'REBAR_GATE_TMPDIR\|e TMPDIR=\|REBAR_GATE_FREE_WATERMARK_PCT' infra/scripts/autodeploy.sh` reporting 3.
- [ ] `mcp_run_new` binds the scratch volume at the parent path. Verified by `grep -q '/var/lib/rebar:/var/lib/rebar' infra/scripts/autodeploy.sh` exiting 0.
- [ ] `tests/unit/test_gate_scratch_volume_aa40.py` asserts the compose mcp service and autodeploy's MCP run path each carry all four settings with matching values. Verified by reading the added assertions and confirming each names the mcp service or autodeploy.
- [ ] Those new assertions fail against the pre-fix tree. Verified by reverting only the compose and autodeploy changes, running `pytest tests/unit/test_gate_scratch_volume_aa40.py`, and recording the non-zero failure count in a comment on this ticket.
- [ ] `pytest tests/unit/test_gate_scratch_volume_aa40.py` reports 0 failures with the fix applied. Verified by the pytest summary line.
- [ ] `docker compose -f infra/compose/docker-compose.yml config --quiet` exits 0, confirming the edited compose file still parses. Verified by the exit code.
- [ ] `bash -n infra/scripts/autodeploy.sh` exits 0, confirming the edited script still parses. Verified by the exit code.
- [ ] `make lint` and `make typecheck` pass. Verified by both exiting 0.

file_impact.reason: The mcp service sets none of the four gate-scratch settings; they exist only under review-bot. Adding them here makes compose the single source the autodeploy run path and the parity test pin against.
mcp_run_new creates the live blue-green MCP containers and sets none of the four settings, so gate snapshots land on the container writable layer.

Existing parity test pinning the gate-scratch mount across compose, terraform and observability.sh, but only for the service that already had the settings. Extended to cover the compose mcp service and autodeploy's MCP run path.
